9	### Simple algebras
10	
11	This is the [Setoid.Congruences.Simple][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	Classically, a *nontrivial* algebra is **simple** when its congruence lattice has
14	exactly two members: the diagonal, which relates only the setoid-equal pairs, and
15	the total congruence, which relates everything.  This module defines *simple*
16	as an implication, and keeps nontriviality out of the definition.[^1]
17	
18	The module develops the following:
19	
20	+  `RelatesDistinctPoints`{.AgdaFunction}: the positive data of a binary relation
21	   (in use, the relation of a congruence) relating a pair of provably distinct
22	   elements;
23	+  `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction}, the implication definition of "simple algebra": a
24	   congruence relating a distinct pair relates every pair;
25	+  `trivial⇒simple`{.AgdaFunction}: the trivial algebra is simple vacuously;
26	+  `simple⇒total`{.AgdaFunction}: in a simple algebra, a congruence relating a
27	   distinct pair is the total congruence;
28	+  `nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero`{.AgdaFunction} and `simple⇒si`{.AgdaFunction}: a
29	   nontrivial simple algebra is subdirectly irreducible with the total congruence
30	   as its monolith, under a witness-extraction antecedent that the design note
31	   below explains.
32	
33	The group-theoretic special case is `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of
34	[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][]; the identification of the two notions
35	through the normal-subgroup ↔ congruence correspondence is proved in
36	[Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences][].
37	
38	#### Design note: the implication form
39	
40	The textbook definition of a simple algebra classifies every congruence as
41	either the diagonal or the total congruence.  Stated over arbitrary congruences,
42	that disjunction is oracle-strength data, for exactly the reason recorded in
43	[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] and
44	[Classical.Structures.Group.MaximalSubgroup][]: relatedness under a congruence can
45	encode an arbitrary proposition, which the classifier would decide up to double
46	negation, and no concrete algebra with two provably distinct elements could
47	inhabit the disjunctive form in `--safe` Agda.  The definition here is therefore
48	an implication: if a congruence relates a pair of provably distinct elements,
49	then it relates every pair.
50	
51	Two further choices mirror the group module.
52	
53	+  **The witnessed pair is positive data**.  The hypothesis is the type
54	   `RelatesDistinctPoints`{.AgdaFunction}, an inhabitant of which is a pair
55	   packaged with its relatedness and distinctness proofs; this is deliberately not
56	   of the same shape as `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction} in [Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][];
57	   the latter is a negation and carries no witness.  Consumers apply simplicity by
58	   producing the pair along with its relatedness and distinctness proofs.  The
59	   group-side equivalence of [Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences][] produces
60	   it from a non-identity member of a normal subgroup.
61	+  **Nontriviality stays out of the definition**.  The trivial algebra inhabits
62	   the implication form vacuously (`trivial⇒simple`{.AgdaFunction}); nontriviality
63	   witnesses live in bundles, exactly as `IsNonabelianSimple`{.AgdaRecord} handles
64	   the group side.
65	
66	The implication form does not recover the disjunctive classification (a congruence
67	is either the diagonal or relates all pairs); deciding which disjunct
68	holds would decide, for an arbitrary congruence, whether it relates a distinct
69	pair.  The fact that the disjunctive readings (both here and on the group side)
70	are unreachable from the form that concrete instances inhabit is strong evidence
71	that the implication form is the right primitive.
72	
73	??? note "A note on universe levels"
74	
75	    `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} takes the congruence level `ℓ` as a parameter and
76	    quantifies over `Con`{.AgdaFunction}` 𝑨 ℓ` at that level, the same per-level
77	    discipline as the correspondence of [Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences][].
78	    The subdirect-irreducibility facts in this module instantiate it at the
79	    algebra's own relation level `ρ`, where the monolith vocabulary of
80	    [Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][] lives; the group-side equivalence instantiates
81	    it at the level `α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀` of the group's subgroup predicates.

111	#### Definition: simple algebra
112	
113	Fix an algebra `𝑨`.  The hypothesis a consumer supplies is a related pair together
114	with a proof that the setoid equality distinguishes the two elements of the pair.
115	It is stated for an arbitrary binary relation on the carrier, since only the
116	relation of a congruence is ever inspected; everything below applies it to that
117	relation.
118	
119	```agda
120	module _ (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) where
121	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]  using ( _≈_ )
122	
123	  -- The positive data: θ relates a pair of provably distinct elements.
124	  RelatesDistinctPoints : BinaryRel 𝕌[ 𝑨 ] ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
125	  RelatesDistinctPoints _θ_ = ∃[ a ] ∃[ b ] a θ b × ¬ a ≈ b
126	```

128	An algebra is **simple** provided every congruence relating a pair of distinct
129	elements relates every pair.  (The trivial algebra satisfies the definition
130	vacuously.)
131	
132	```agda
133	  -- Simple algebra, implication form: a congruence relating a pair of
134	  -- provably distinct elements relates every pair.
135	  IsSimple : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ)
136	  IsSimple ℓ = ((_θ_ , _) : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → RelatesDistinctPoints _θ_ → ∀ x y → x θ y
137	```
138	
139	In the trivial algebra no congruence relates a distinct pair, so the hypothesis is
140	refutable and the implication holds vacuously; this is the formal record of the
141	decision to keep nontriviality out of the definition.
142	
143	```agda
144	  -- The trivial algebra is simple vacuously: no congruence relates a distinct pair.
145	  trivial⇒simple : Trivial 𝑨 → IsSimple ℓ
146	  trivial⇒simple triv θ (a , b , _ , a≉b) = ⊥-elim (a≉b (triv a b))
147	```

149	#### Exactly two congruences, positively
150	
151	The disjunctive slogan survives in the form concrete instances can use: a congruence
152	of a simple algebra that relates a distinct pair is the total congruence
153	`𝟙[ 𝑨 ]`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Basic][], up to the mutual
154	containment `≑`{.AgdaFunction} that serves as equality of congruences.
155	
156	```agda
157	  -- A congruence of a simple algebra relating a distinct pair is the total
158	  -- congruence.
159	  simple⇒total : IsSimple ℓ → (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → RelatesDistinctPoints (proj₁ θ) → θ ≑ 𝟙[ 𝑨 ]
160	  simple⇒total simp θ wit = (λ _ → lift tt) , λ {x} {y} _ → simp θ wit x y
161	```

163	#### Relation to subdirect irreducibility
164	
165	A nontrivial simple algebra is subdirectly irreducible, and its monolith is the
166	total congruence: every nonzero congruence is in fact total, so the total
167	congruence is the least nonzero one.
168	
169	One step of this argument is not constructive.  The field `mono-least`{.AgdaField}
170	of `IsMonolith`{.AgdaRecord} consumes `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction}, which is a
171	negation, while simplicity consumes the positive
172	`RelatesDistinctPoints`{.AgdaFunction} data, and extracting the witness from the
173	negation is a double-negation elimination.  The statement below therefore isolates
174	that step as an antecedent, a witness-extraction principle for nonzero
175	congruences, exactly as `Stable-≈ε`{.AgdaFunction} isolates the classical step in
176	[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][].  The antecedent can be discharged by a
177	finite search wherever the congruences concerned are pointwise decidable over an

179	[Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormalDescent][].  No such instance is built
180	here; the halves that are constructive outright are stated separately, so a
181	consumer holding positive data never pays for the extraction.

183	```agda
184	  -- In a nontrivial algebra the total congruence is nonzero.
185	  nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero : Nontrivial 𝑨 → Nonzero 𝑨 (𝟙[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ})
186	  nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero (a , b , a≉b) 𝟙⊆Δ = a≉b (𝟙⊆Δ (lift tt))
187	```
188	
189	Assembling the pieces under the antecedent: nontriviality makes the total
190	congruence nonzero, extraction turns any nonzero congruence into a witnessed one,
191	and simplicity makes every witnessed congruence total, so the total congruence is
192	the least nonzero congruence, which is exactly the monolith.
193	
194	```agda
195	  -- With a witness-extraction principle for nonzero congruences, a nontrivial
196	  -- simple algebra is subdirectly irreducible, with the total congruence as
197	  -- its monolith.
198	  simple⇒si : Nontrivial 𝑨 → IsSimple ρ
199	    →  ((θ : Con 𝑨 ρ) → Nonzero 𝑨 θ → RelatesDistinctPoints (proj₁ θ))
200	    →  IsSubdirectlyIrreducible 𝑨
201	  simple⇒si A-nt A-simp θ-rdp = A-nt , 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] , 𝟙-isMonolith
202	    where
203	    𝟙-isMonolith : IsMonolith 𝑨 𝟙[ 𝑨 ]
204	    𝟙-isMonolith =
205	      record  { mono-nonzero = nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero A-nt
206	              ; mono-least = λ θ nz {x}{y} _ → A-simp θ (θ-rdp θ nz) x y }
207	```
208

212	      vacuously (`trivial⇒simple`{.AgdaFunction}; see the design note below).

#### Definition: simple algebra

Fix an algebra `𝑨`.  The hypothesis a consumer supplies is a related pair together
with a proof that the setoid equality distinguishes the two elements of the pair.
It is stated for an arbitrary binary relation on the carrier, since only the
relation of a congruence is ever inspected; everything below applies it to that
relation.

```agda
module _ (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) where
  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]  using ( _≈_ )

  -- The positive data: θ relates a pair of provably distinct elements.
  RelatesDistinctPoints : BinaryRel 𝕌[ 𝑨 ] ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  RelatesDistinctPoints _θ_ = ∃[ a ] ∃[ b ] a θ b × ¬ a ≈ b
```

An algebra is **simple** provided every congruence relating a pair of distinct
elements relates every pair.  (The trivial algebra satisfies the definition
vacuously.)

```agda
  -- Simple algebra, implication form: a congruence relating a pair of
  -- provably distinct elements relates every pair.
  IsSimple : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ)
  IsSimple ℓ = ((_θ_ , _) : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → RelatesDistinctPoints _θ_ → ∀ x y → x θ y
```

In the trivial algebra no congruence relates a distinct pair, so the hypothesis is
refutable and the implication holds vacuously; this is the formal record of the
decision to keep nontriviality out of the definition.

```agda
  -- The trivial algebra is simple vacuously: no congruence relates a distinct pair.
  trivial⇒simple : Trivial 𝑨 → IsSimple ℓ
  trivial⇒simple triv θ (a , b , _ , a≉b) = ⊥-elim (a≉b (triv a b))
```

of a simple algebra that relates a distinct pair is the total congruence
`𝟙[ 𝑨 ]`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Basic][], up to the mutual
containment `≑`{.AgdaFunction} that serves as equality of congruences.

```agda
  -- A congruence of a simple algebra relating a distinct pair is the total
  -- congruence.
  simple⇒total : IsSimple ℓ → (θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → RelatesDistinctPoints (proj₁ θ) → θ ≑ 𝟙[ 𝑨 ]
  simple⇒total simp θ wit = (λ _ → lift tt) , λ {x} {y} _ → simp θ wit x y
```

#### Relation to subdirect irreducibility

A nontrivial simple algebra is subdirectly irreducible, and its monolith is the
total congruence: every nonzero congruence is in fact total, so the total
congruence is the least nonzero one.

One step of this argument is not constructive.  The field `mono-least`{.AgdaField}
of `IsMonolith`{.AgdaRecord} consumes `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction}, which is a
negation, while simplicity consumes the positive
`RelatesDistinctPoints`{.AgdaFunction} data, and extracting the witness from the
negation is a double-negation elimination.  The statement below therefore isolates
that step as an antecedent, a witness-extraction principle for nonzero
congruences, exactly as `Stable-≈ε`{.AgdaFunction} isolates the classical step in
[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][].  The antecedent can be discharged by a
finite search wherever the congruences concerned are pointwise decidable over an
enumerated carrier; this is the approach `witness`{.AgdaFunction} takes in
[Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormalDescent][].  No such instance is built
here; the halves that are constructive outright are stated separately, so a
consumer holding positive data never pays for the extraction.

```agda
  -- In a nontrivial algebra the total congruence is nonzero.
  nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero : Nontrivial 𝑨 → Nonzero 𝑨 (𝟙[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ})
  nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero (a , b , a≉b) 𝟙⊆Δ = a≉b (𝟙⊆Δ (lift tt))
```

Assembling the pieces under the antecedent: nontriviality makes the total
congruence nonzero, extraction turns any nonzero congruence into a witnessed one,
and simplicity makes every witnessed congruence total, so the total congruence is
the least nonzero congruence, which is exactly the monolith.

```agda
  -- With a witness-extraction principle for nonzero congruences, a nontrivial
  -- simple algebra is subdirectly irreducible, with the total congruence as
  -- its monolith.
  simple⇒si : Nontrivial 𝑨 → IsSimple ρ
    →  ((θ : Con 𝑨 ρ) → Nonzero 𝑨 θ → RelatesDistinctPoints (proj₁ θ))
    →  IsSubdirectlyIrreducible 𝑨
  simple⇒si A-nt A-simp θ-rdp = A-nt , 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] , 𝟙-isMonolith
    where
    𝟙-isMonolith : IsMonolith 𝑨 𝟙[ 𝑨 ]
    𝟙-isMonolith =
      record  { mono-nonzero = nontrivial⇒𝟙-nonzero A-nt
              ; mono-least = λ θ nz {x}{y} _ → A-simp θ (θ-rdp θ nz) x y }
```

---

[^1]: The trivial algebra, whose diagonal and total congruences coincide, is simple
      vacuously (`trivial⇒simple`{.AgdaFunction}; see the design note below).

#### The Congruence Lattice of a Setoid Algebra

This is the [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

The congruences of an algebra `𝑨`, ordered by containment, form a complete lattice.
This module begins the formalization of that fact by promoting `Con 𝑨` to a
first-class ordered object: it defines the containment order `_⊆_`, the induced
equivalence `_≑_` of mutual containment, and the **meet** `θ ∧ φ`, which is the
relational intersection `θ ∩ φ`.  The intersection of two congruences is again a
congruence, and it is the greatest lower bound of the two arguments.  Thus we have a
partially ordered set which, with the meet operation, forms a semilattice.

<!--

```agda
-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------
open import Agda.Primitive           using () renaming ( Set to Type )
open import Data.Product             using ( _×_ ; _,_ ; proj₁ ; proj₂ ; swap )
open import Data.Unit.Base           using ( tt )
open import Level                    using ( Level ; _⊔_ ; lift ; lower )
open import Relation.Binary          using ( Setoid ; IsEquivalence ; IsPartialOrder ; _⇒_ )
                                     renaming ( Rel to BinaryRel )
open import Relation.Binary.Bundles  using ( Poset )
open import Relation.Binary.Lattice  using ( Infimum ; IsMeetSemilattice ; MeetSemilattice )

-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebras Library ------------------------------
open import Overture                  using  ( 𝑆 )
open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic     using  ( ov ; Algebra ; 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Basic  using  ( Con ; mkcon ; _∣≈_ ; reflexive
                                             ; is-equivalence ; is-compatible
                                             ; 𝟘[_] ; 𝟙[_] )
private variable α ρ ℓ : Level
```
